messages:
alice: kicking off canary for billing-service v3.7.2 in change window 23:00-00:00 UTC. routing 10% traffic to canary. please monitor p95 and error-rate. link to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/backout-billing-service

deploybot: Deploy started by alice. canary=10% target hosts=billing-canary-01..03. CI: green. (build 3782) :rocket:

ben: noted. will watch observability dashboard. added alert for error_rate>0.8% for 5m and p95>1.2s. :eyes:

carol: If we hit threshold, follow runbook 'billing-backout-quick' — steps 1-3. Quick snippet:
```
# backout quick actions
kubectl scale deployment billing-canary --replicas=0
kubectl set image deployment/billing stable=billing:3.7.1
kubectl rollout status deployment/billing
```

alice: also pin routing in the router config if we decide to rollback: set route weight 100->stable via /infra/router config. I'll keep the pin PR ready.

dave: noted. I pushed a rollback playbook gist with the exact pin command and checks: https://gist.github.com/dave/rollback-billing-192

sre-bot: Observability: no spike yet. p95=720ms, error_rate=0.12% (1m)

ben: if we see tail latency in logs, don't attempt multiple restarts — follow runbook section 'do-not-flap' to avoid thrashing.

carol: reminder: change window ops contact is @alice; escalation to pager if rollback needed after 3 mins of sustained breach. Also follow the safety cutoff: don't attempt DB migrations rollback without lead.

alice: can we approve fail-open mode for feature flag if partial degradation? yes/no

ben: approve fail-open for payments-readonly only. do not enable for write paths.

alice: thanks. will report back. :thumbsup:

deploybot: Canary reached 10% stable. monitoring for 20m baseline.

sre-bot: alerting policy linked: https://redwood.internal/alerts/deploys/billing-canary

alice: closing thread — will post update at end of window or on any rollback.
